strategy.summary: Kantteile Strasser is a small, sound, founder-owned Austrian sheet-metal shop with 25 staff. It supplies part:330030 (motor bracket) at a 50% quota under a framework contract. It is qualified for part:330020 at 0% quota. It has idle capacity: the second shift has been on hold since spring. It values Hollerau as a reference customer, and the owner prices from a stale spreadsheet. It has never won an increase on 330030 in three renewals and is dearer than the second source Steinfelder. Delivery (76% on time against a 95% target) and quality (762 ppm against a 457 peer median, open 8Ds on leakage) are weak. Leverage is ours. The best currency is volume and quota, including a 330020 share, plus on-time payment, rather than price pressure alone. Its steel-driven cost claim of about +3% is checkable but weak in context. There is no should-cost, so the margin evidence is thin.

The index-backed claim is real but modest and its context is weak, with steel still below the 2023 peak. There is no should-cost, so the margin is unknown. Aim to hold the current price or move toward the rival level in exchange for volume.

findings.text: No should-cost exists for either part, so the margin over full cost cannot be measured. Price room can only be judged from the rival price, past quotes and index movements. The evidence on margin is thin.

Part 330030 (motor bracket): Strasser has charged EUR 16.11 since 2024, flat for three years after a -6% cut from 17.13. The second source Steinfelder supplies the same part at EUR 15.63, so Strasser is 3.0% dearer. Strasser won the 2025 RFQ at 16.90 against Steinfelder's 16.70 and then kept 16.11. A realistic target is to hold 16.11 or move toward 15.6-15.9.

Part 330020 (coupling guard): Strasser lost the 2025 benchmark at EUR 21.00 against Steinfelder's 20.00, and its lead time was longer (30 vs 21 days). Steinfelder now quotes and sells at 18.16, about 13.5% below Strasser's last quote. If Strasser bids for this part, it has to land near or below 18.16.

The weighted 12-month cost drivers give Strasser about +2.9% on 330020 (steel +2.29%, labour +0.82%, power -0.04%) and about +2.8% on 330030 (+2.29%, +0.67%, -0.15%). Steel is still 6.3% below its 36-month peak and 26.7% below its 2022 high. Prices were set in 2023 near that peak and have been cut only modestly since. A claim of up to roughly +3% is index-backed on paper but weak in context.

Strasser will likely cite the steel move since its 2025-12 low (+7.8%, about +2.74%) and the news of steel +7.3% since January. That window is cherry-picked; the 12-month figure of +6.5% is the fair one to answer with. Copper, electronics and alloy-surcharge news have no bearing on carbon-steel sheet parts (DX51D/S235JR).

Strasser historically settles about 3.4 percentage points below its ask (last ask +3.6%, settled 0%). Its owner prices from a spreadsheet last updated two years ago, and it has idle capacity (second shift on hold). Together these suggest its quotes are not cost-tight and that it has a volume appetite.

findings.text: Small founder-owned Austrian sheet-metal shop (25 staff, 2-5 M EUR turnover). The owner himself decides on price and talks to us directly. There is no corporate approval ladder: decisions are fast and personal.

The owner's costing is stale. He works from his own spreadsheet, last updated about two years ago, and asked us where our index figures come from. He is unsure of his own cost basis, so checkable index data framed helpfully can anchor the talks. Do not humiliate him: as founder he is likely sensitive to being shown up.

Idle capacity. The second shift has been on hold since spring, and sales offered to take additional parts at short notice. They need volume and utilisation more than price. Shifting quota (e.g. 330030 is at 50%, 330020 at 0%) is the trade they value most.

They need recognition and the relationship. At the supplier day they called Hollerau an important reference customer, so reputation and continuity matter to them beyond our spend of about 4.2% of their turnover.
They are financially sound: equity ratio 31.1% and credit index 223, unchanged over 12 months. There is no financial-stress red flag, but they can afford to walk away if pushed too hard.

Our payment record is a sensitivity on our side. 87.8% of invoices are paid late, by 4.6 days on average and up to 15 days, against 30-day terms. They may raise it or ask for faster payment. Paying on time, or sooner, is a cheap concession for a small firm.
They communicate little: there is no recorded price letter or complaint, only an ISO certificate e-mail. Persona evidence is thin overall.

findings.text: Framework contract covers only part:330030 (Motor bracket HB). Prices are fixed per calendar year, and any change needs written notice at least 90 days before year end, so by about 2 Oct for 2027. Payment is 30 days net against our 60-day standard, which is already a concession to them. Delivery is DAP with a 28-day lead time.
The contract runs 2025-07-01 to 2027-06-30 and extends automatically by 12 months unless terminated with 90 days' notice. Notice by 2027-04-01 stops the renewal, so a credible exit remains open.

History on 330030: it asked -3.1% and settled -6% (2023), asked +3.7% and settled 0 (2024), asked +3.6% and settled 0 (2025). It has never achieved an increase. The price is 16.11, down from 17.13, and has been flat since 2024.

Dual sourcing on 330030 is 50/50 with Steinfelder, which we currently pay EUR 15.63, below Strasser's 16.11. Hollerau owns the tooling. Strasser won the 2025 benchmark RFQ against Steinfelder's 16.70 quote.
On part 330020 Strasser is qualified but holds a 0% quota. Steinfelder has 100%, Hollerau owns the tooling, and Steinfelder won the 2025 RFQ. This is a possible bundling carrot for Strasser.

Mutual dependency:
- Our side: spend is about EUR 148k, roughly 4.2% of their turnover. They call us an important reference customer and have idle capacity, with the second shift on hold.
- Their side: the supplier is financially sound (equity 31%, credit index stable).
- Weak spot on our side: we pay on average 4.6 days late on 87.8% of invoices.

findings.text: Delivery is improving but still well short of target: rolling OTD against requested date rose from 51.9% (2024Q4) to 80% (2026Q1), then slipped back to 76% in 2026Q2-Q3. Target is 95%, peer median 84.6%. When late, it averages 13.7 days late, with a maximum of 23 days, against a 28-day standard lead time. Even against its own confirmed dates it reaches only 84%.

Quality is persistently weak at about 760 ppm rolling, against a peer median of 457. The trend is flat: 771 ppm a year earlier, 640 at best in 2026Q2. Defects keep recurring: coating defect, leakage at test and dimension. The two newest QNs (2026-07-19 and 2026-08-20) have no D8 date, and one 8D is overdue in the scorecard. Leakage at test is a pump-critical defect. Recharges are only EUR 150 flat per complaint, about EUR 2,250 in total, which does not deter recurrence.

It supplies only part:330030 (motor bracket), on a 50/50 split with sup:70340. The second source is cheaper (15.63 vs 16.11, -3%) and has a similar ppm (870 vs 762). Strasser's price has been flat at 16.11 since 2024.

Volume outlook for 330030 is stable to slightly up: the 2026-09 forecast is 18,790 against 18,360 ordered in the last 12 months, and the forecast is shared with suppliers. Strasser's half is about 9,300 pcs a year. It has spare capacity (second shift on hold), so extra quota is valuable to it and is our main trade currency.

Our ordering contributes to its delivery problem: 8 rush lines, 6 partial deliveries, and 8 lines confirmed later than requested. Its case also has support from our late payments (4.6 days late on average) and its earlier price cuts (-6% since 2023).
part:330020 is not supplied by Strasser today: quota 0%, with sup:70340 at 100%. It is a possible bundling or quota-gain lever. Performance evidence for Strasser on 330020 is absent.

arguments.text: Our price has not moved for three years while input costs have risen. We gave -6% in the 2024 renewal and held flat in 2025 and 2026, even though we asked for +3.7% and +3.6%. Since then steel is up 6.5% year on year and labour 2.7%. On your own driver weights (steel 0.35, labour 0.25), that is roughly +3% on cost. We are only asking to recover cost, not to raise our margin.

Our performance has clearly improved. On-time delivery rose from 51.9% to 76%, on-time against confirmed date is 84%, and ppm fell from about 1,033 to 762. We reached class A in 2026Q1. Our ppm on 330030 (762) is now better than your second source Steinfelder's (870) on the same part.

We are a long-standing, reliable partner. We have supplied 330030 since 2013 and are a dual source that protects your supply. We are small and founder-owned, and an equity ratio of 31% has to be sustained with a fair margin.
You pay most of our invoices late: 87.8% are paid after the due date, about 5 days late on average. For a firm of 25 people that is real financing cost on our side.
The gap to Steinfelder is small. In the July 2025 benchmark we won the award on this part at 16.90, even though Steinfelder quoted 16.70. So the price difference alone did not decide it.

weak_points: We have never won an increase in three renewals, and they know our asks end at zero.
We are 0.48 EUR (about 3%) dearer than Steinfelder on 330030.
On-time delivery of 76% is still far below the 95% target, and late deliveries average about 14 days.
There are open 8Ds on leakage and coating (qn:20004979, qn:20004996), with recurring leakage at test.
The second shift is idle and our sales staff told them we would take parts at short notice. That shows we need volume.
The owner's cost spreadsheet is two years old, so our cost basis may not hold up if they probe it.
Electricity prices are down 3.7% year on year and steel is still 6.3% below its 2023 peak.
We lost 330020 on price in the 2025 benchmark (21 vs 20).
The framework contract fixes prices per calendar year and requires 90 days' notice. If notice was missed, the 2027 price is locked.
wants: A higher quota on 330030, for example 60-70% instead of 50%.
A share of 330020: we are qualified but currently at 0%, with about 15,000 pcs per year in the forecast.
Binding annual volume and a longer contract term to justify restarting the second shift.
On-time payment, or a shorter payment term.
For that volume, we could hold the price flat or even match about 15.9 on 330030 and quote 330020 near 18.2.
Something modest on index or steel, such as a steel index clause in place of an increase.
red_lines: No price cut below about the Steinfelder level (around 15.6) without a volume increase.
No ppm or chargeback commitments we cannot meet, such as a penalty above 150 EUR per complaint or a very tight ppm target.
No lead time below about 21 days without a firm forecast.
Losing the 330030 quota entirely is unacceptable, so we would concede rather than walk away.
red_team.opening: Thank Hollerau for the partnership and the supplier day. Show the improvement in delivery and quality. Point out three years of flat or reduced prices against steel up 6.5% and labour up 2.7%, and ask for +3.5% on 330030. At the same time, signal openly that we have capacity. Offer to hold the price flat if Hollerau raises our 330030 quota and gives us a share of 330020 under a binding volume and a longer term, with payment on time.

rebuttals.answer: You are right that steel and labour have risen over the past year, and we take that seriously. Put in proportion, though: weighted by their share of the part, the two drivers support only a modest change, and power has fallen over the same period, which offsets part of it. The steel figure is also a recovery from a low, not a new high. Our current price is the reference point, and the second source supplies the same bracket for less today. Rather than a cost pass-through, we would prefer to give you more work and a longer commitment, which helps your costs more than a price step would. We are also happy to share the index sources we use, so we both work from the same basis.

We have noticed the improvement and we appreciate it: delivery and ppm are clearly better than a year ago. The rolling figures are still well short of what we agreed, though. On-time delivery is far from the contract target and below the peer median. We see this as a joint improvement plan to finish, not yet as grounds for a premium.

We value the long partnership and your role as a dual source, and we want you healthy. Your finances look sound and stable, and the best support we can offer a firm with free capacity is volume and planning security rather than a higher unit price. That is the conversation we would like to have.

That is a fair point, and we will not argue it. We commit to paying on time from now on, and we will put that commitment in writing. The delays have been short on average, so the financing effect is small next to the unit price, and we would rather fix the cause than compensate for it through the price.

That award reflected the whole picture at the time, and we were glad to place it with you. Since then the order book shows the second source supplying the same part for less, and its delivery has been more reliable. A gap of this size on a shared part matters when we decide how to split future volume. We would like to close it together, in exchange for a bigger share.

press: We understand your second shift has capacity available, and we would like to explore how a larger share of the bracket could help fill it at today's price.
If you can come closer to market level, we would also be glad to invite you to quote the coupling guard, where our shared forecast shows growing volume.
We would welcome a plan to bring on-time delivery up toward the contract target, since reliability is what would let us place more volume with you.
As agreed in our framework contract, prices are fixed per calendar year, so we would suggest we discuss any change within that framework.
A longer commitment with binding volume might help your planning; would that be worth more to you than a price change?
